title: Compact INT8/FP8 kernel routing and prefill scheduler to reduce dequantization overhead
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Design and implement a compact kernel-routing layer plus a prefill-aware scheduler that minimizes cross-format dequantization and memory traffic for INT8/FP8 mixed-precision paths. This ticket covers the design, prototype kernels (fused dequant+attention epilogue), scheduler heuristics, and perf validation on representative workloads (chatty decode and long-context prefill).
background: We already have multiple quantized execution paths, but runtime currently incurs repeated dequant/ requant copies when requests traverse components optimized for different precision formats. This is especially costly for (1) prefill-heavy workloads with large KV cache writes and (2) mixed workloads that switch between INT8-prefilled keys and FP8 decode kernels. Previous tickets focused on individual kernel optimizations; this work stitches a routing and scheduling layer to avoid redundant conversions and reduce memory bandwidth pressure.
decision_summary: Adopt a hybrid approach: (A) introduce a lightweight kernel multiplexor that selects a fused path when a whole-request precision is compatible, and (B) add a prefill scheduler that batches prefill writes by precision bucket to maximize reuse of on-device quantized KV blocks. Where full fusion isn't possible, use zero-copy aliasing + in-place requant to avoid extra roundtrips.
tradeoffs: Complexity: multiplexor adds routing logic per-request which increases code surface and test matrix.
Compatibility: not every model or backend supports fused kernels; fallbacks required.
Memory vs Latency: keeping multiple quantized representations increases memory but reduces repeated conversion latency.
Engineering time: prototype + verification estimated at ~5 points; kernel vendors may need microkernel support.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end regression tests for chat and prefill flows pass with fused and fallback paths.
Perf: >=12% median decode latency reduction on representative chat workload compared to current master (same hardware).
Perf: >=8% token/s throughput improvement for mixed precision scenarios on A100 80GB and AWS g5.4xlarge (or equivalent).
No functional accuracy regressions on our eval suite (top-k/top-p distributions within historical baselines).
Operational: new telemetry exposes per-request routing decision and KV write precision histogram in Console.
Safe fallback: when backend lacks fused kernel, system uses zero-copy path without extra copies.
implementation_plan: Design phase: finalize routing heuristics (sequence-length thresholds, kv-cache occupancy trigger, per-route precision hints) — owner: Asha (2 days).
Prototype fused epilogue: implement dequant+attention epilogue for INT8->FP16/FP8 decode on CUDA (PR draft) — owner: Liam (1 week).
Prefill scheduler: add scheduler that groups prefill writes by target quant format and staggers large prefill writes to allow batching — owner: Mei Chen (3 days).
Zero-copy aliasing: implement buffer aliasing and in-place requant where safe; update allocator to track quant format metadata — owner: Marcos Silva (4 days).
Integration & tests: add unit tests, end-to-end perf harness, console telemetry and feature flag gating — owner: QA & Observability (3 days).
Rollout: gated rollout behind feature flag with canary on Dedicated clusters, collect perf signals for two weeks before full rollout.
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting; confirmed perf goals and available hardware for benchmarks (A100 + Ampere MIG + g5 instances).
2026-02-22: Prototype fused epilogue submitted as draft (link below). Microbenchmarks show ~18% reduction in epilogue memory bandwidth on synthetic attention with 2k sequence length.
2026-03-02: Early integration of multiplexor in runtime; added per-request hint header to API to prefer 'quant-fused' paths. Initial correctness tests green.
2026-03-08: Prefill scheduler algorithm v0 implemented — groups prefill writes by precision and issues them in two-stage commit to KV cache. Observed fewer requant operations in trace logs.

2026-03-12: End-to-end bench on chat synthetic workload: median decode latency down 14% vs master, peak token/s up 10%. Identified edge-case when mixed-precision attention dropout path falls back to scalar slow path (follow-up).
benchmarks: Setup: A100 40GB, model: 7B baseline quantized INT8 path, workloads: chat-8k (interactive decode) and long-prefill-16k.
Chat-8k: median decode latency -14%, 95th percentile -9%; token/s +10%.
Long-prefill-16k: prefill phase walltime -18% due to batched quantized KV writes; end-to-end memory bandwidth down ~28% on epilogue-heavy runs.
Mixed workload: token/s +8% and measured reduction in repeated dequant ops by 65% in traces after scheduler grouping.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Some third-party kernels do not expose hooks for fused epilogues. Mitigation: implement zero-copy aliasing as fallback and work with vendor teams to upstream hooks.
Risk: Increased memory usage when keeping multiple quantized representations. Mitigation: LRU purging of alternate representations and heuristics that only keep representations for hot KV shards.
Risk: Accuracy divergence in FP8 paths. Mitigation: run full eval suite and enable runtime precision monitoring with auto-fallback if quality drifts beyond threshold.
review_feedback: 2026-02-25 (Nina Gupta): Prefer explicit per-model precision policy rather than per-route heuristics to avoid surprising routing in enterprise tenants. Action: add per-model override in mux config.
2026-03-05 (Platform SLA team): Request that fused path has a deterministic timeout to avoid blocking autoscaler signals. Action: add 50ms fallback timer in scheduler.
2026-03-11 (Applied ML): Run additional evaluation on instruction-following prompts to ensure no FP8 tail behavior causes subtle distribution shifts.
